meta.atr: Wilder ATR14 (alpha=1/14) on M5 bars (70-minute window), recomputed from raw CSV
meta.note: data ends 2026-08-04 — static research export, no model, no live feed

definitions.avg_range_atr: mean((H-L)/ATR14[t]) of bars in the slot
definitions.avg_range_usd: mean(H-L) in USD (gold: price units ARE USD; point = 0.01, spread points x 0.01 = USD)
definitions.p_high_vol_empirical: share of bars where next bar's range > 1.2 x ATR14[t]
definitions.bar_count: raw bars in the slot over the full history

hourly.note: Gold trades 23h/day: hour_utc 0 is absent (session break 00:00-01:00 UTC) — its stats are null with bar_count 0. Same definitions as sessions.json.

highlights.quietest_slot_note: quietest among slots with >100 bars (same filter as the research findings)
highlights.ny_vs_asia_note: mean bar range in ATR units: NY band (1.0996x ATR) vs Asia band (1.008x ATR), full M5 history

econ.trade_model: 1:2 RR, SL = 1xATR14, TP = 2xATR14, entry cost = spread; breakeven win% p* = (1 + spread/ATR) / 3
econ.verdict: M5 ECON NOT SURVIVABLE (worse than gold M15): median spread is 4.8% of ATR (1.9x the M15 ratio of 2.5%), pushing the 1:2-RR breakeven win rate to 34.9% — +1.5pp over the 33.4% the verified gold H1 system actually achieved (M15 needed only +0.7pp). The spread tax hits M5 roughly 1.9x harder than M15 — and this export carries no directional edge, only the clock.

guidance.hot_slots: Hottest slots (e.g. 15:30 UTC, US session: 2.2x ATR, 64% high-vol hit rate): size down or widen SL — gold's volatility is predictable by the clock, direction is not. A 2x-ATR M5 bar cuts both ways.
guidance.quiet_slots: Quiet slots (late-day drift, e.g. 23:20 UTC at 0.6x ATR): poor RR environment — the spread eats small ranges, so expected value after costs is worse than the raw calm suggests.
guidance.economics: Median spread is 4.8% of ATR and 2.68% of bars have spread > 25% of ATR. Breakeven at 1:2 RR needs 34.9% wins vs the 33.4% gold Phase-3 reference — a +1.5pp tax, WORSE than gold M15 (+0.7pp): M5 econ is NOT survivable on its own, prefer M15 timing. The clock tells you WHEN gold moves, not WHICH WAY.
guidance.general: M5 gold scalping is a downgrade from M15 on costs: the median M5 ATR is only $1.62 against a $0.09 median spread, so the fixed spread consumes 4.8% of the bar's range (vs 2.5% at M15). If you scalp gold at all, use the M15 clock; use M5 only in the cheapest windows and only with a real directional edge. This is a static research export, not a signal service: volatility by slot is an empirical average over 2022-2026, not a forecast for any specific day.
